approach: The linked repository contains only the raw CDR CSV, so the whole pipeline is rebuilt from the paper's Section III description using scikit-learn + imbalanced-learn (+ xgboost for C6/C7). One data module loads the CSV (from the cloned repo, or a raw GitHub download if the clone is absent), drops rows with missing values, drops the unique phone-number identifier, label-encodes the categorical state/plan fields, applies Min-Max scaling per Eq. 1, applies SMOTE with default 1:1 balancing, then splits 80/20 — the paper's stated order (A1/A8), which puts synthetic minority points in the test set and is the only ordering consistent with a 99.9% RF result. A second, leak-free variant (split first, SMOTE only on the training fold, scaler fit on train) is run alongside and reported as an honest lower bound, since the paper's ordering is a known defect. Random Forest (scikit-learn defaults, A3) and XGBoost (library defaults, A4) are fit over five fixed seeds; accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and ROC AUC are computed with fraud as the positive class (Eqs. 9-12) plus the confusion matrix, and everything is written to results/metrics.json keyed by claim id with the mean over seeds and per-seed values. C8 is reported but explicitly flagged non-reproducible because the paper's matrix sums to 300,000 predictions for a 101,174-record dataset.

files.purpose: Single dict CONFIG with every hyperparameter, path, seed list and variant definition; imported by all other modules. No magic numbers anywhere else.

Dataset acquisition + preprocessing in the paper's order: locate 'Call Details-Data.csv' in the cloned repo (recursive glob) or download it via requests from the GitHub raw URL if missing; load with pandas; detect the label column (binary column whose positive count == 8830); report and drop rows with any missing value (R1); drop the unique 'phone number' identifier column; label-encode state and binary plan columns (A6); MinMaxScaler to [0,1] on all features (R2, Eq. 1); SMOTE(k_neighbors=5, sampling_strategy=1.0) on the full preprocessed frame (R3); then train_test_split(test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=seed). Also exposes build_leakfree() which does split -> fit scaler on train -> SMOTE on train only, for the secondary variant. Returns X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test plus a dict of dataset statistics.

Factory functions make_rf() and make_xgb() returning the configured estimators (RF: n_estimators=100, criterion='gini', max_depth=None, n_jobs=-1; XGB: n_estimators=100, learning_rate=0.3, max_depth=6, objective='binary:logistic', tree_method='hist', n_jobs=-1), plus evaluate(model, X_test, y_test) returning accuracy (Eq. 9), precision/recall/F1 for the fraud class = 1 (Eqs. 10-12), ROC AUC, and the 2x2 confusion matrix as a dict. xgboost import is guarded: on ImportError the XGB entries are marked 'unavailable' instead of aborting the run.

Orchestrator: loops over CONFIG['variants'] x CONFIG['seeds'] x {RF, XGB}, calls data builders and models, accumulates per-seed metric rows, writes results/metrics.json (mean, std, per-seed list, test-set size, confusion matrix, dataset stats per variant/seed), results/per_seed.csv, a DummyClassifier/most-frequent sanity row, and saves the RF confusion-matrix figure to results/figures/rf_confusion_matrix.png. Maps results onto claim ids C1-C8 with a 'matches_claim' flag using the 1.0-absolute-point tolerance band and a note for C8 that the reported 300,000-prediction matrix is inconsistent with the dataset.

Thin entrypoint: `python reproduce.py` runs the full protocol (all seeds, both variants, both models) and prints the C1-C8 summary table; `python reproduce.py --smoke` runs the reduced smoke configuration; `--variant`, `--seeds`, `--n-estimators` overrides only mutate a copy of CONFIG. Must not contain modelling logic.

config.label_column: auto-detect: binary column whose positive count == 8830 (README calls it 'churners'); fallback name 'Churn' / 'churners'
config.positive_class: fraud/churn = 1 (A9; low-risk, matches Fig. 4 TP=26,127 for class 1)
config.missing_value_policy: dropna(how='any', axis=0) listwise row deletion (R1, paper Sec III.B)
config.dropped_columns: "phone number" (all-unique identifier, A6); any other column with nunique == n_rows auto-dropped
config.categorical_encoding: label/ordinal encoding of 'state' and binary plan columns (label_encode_plans), stated as A6
config.scaler: sklearn MinMaxScaler(feature_range=(0,1)), Eq. 1 (R2); variant 'paper_order' fits it on the full pre-split frame (A1), variant 'leakfree' fits on train only
config.smote_placement: 'before_split' for the primary variant (paper Fig. 1 order, A1/A8); 'train_only' for the leak-free variant
config.rf_params: n_estimators=100, criterion='gini', max_depth=None, min_samples_split=2, min_samples_leaf=1, max_features='sqrt', bootstrap=True, n_jobs=-1 (A3: scikit-learn defaults, unreported in paper)
config.xgb_params: n_estimators=100, learning_rate=0.3, max_depth=6, subsample=1.0, colsample_bytree=1.0, objective='binary:logistic', eval_metric='logloss', tree_method='hist', n_jobs=-1 (A4: library defaults)
config.metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, f1, roc_auc (percent, x100) with fraud=1 positive (R8, R9, R12); average='binary'
config.timing: ~30-120 s per RF fit, ~1-2 min per XGB fit, ~20-40 s per SMOTE pass

steps: Environment setup: `pip install -q imbalanced-learn xgboost` (scikit-learn, pandas, numpy, matplotlib, requests already present); verify `python -c "import sklearn, imblearn, xgboost"` and record versions into results/metrics.json['environment'].

Locate the data: recursively glob the cloned repo for '*.csv' (expected `Call Details-Data.csv`); if not found, `requests.get` the raw GitHub URL (URL-encoded filename) and save to data/raw/. Assert the file is >5 MB and loads with pandas.
Write config.py with the CONFIG dict exactly as specified above.

Write src/data.py. First run it standalone in a diagnostic mode that prints: raw shape, dtypes, per-column null counts, the auto-detected label column and its value counts — assert 101,174 rows, 8,830 positives (R6) or log the discrepancy verbatim.

Implement the paper-order preprocessing: dropna -> drop identifier -> encode categoricals -> MinMaxScaler on all features -> SMOTE(1:1) -> stratified 80/20 split. Return shapes/class counts in a stats dict at every stage.
Implement the leak-free preprocessing path (split -> fit scaler on train -> SMOTE on train only) in the same module, sharing all cleaning code.
Write src/models.py: make_rf, make_xgb, evaluate() returning accuracy/precision/recall/f1/roc_auc in percent plus TP/FP/TN/FN. Include a DummyClassifier(strategy='most_frequent') sanity path.

Write src/run_experiment.py: nested loop over variants x seeds x models, collect rows, aggregate mean/std, build results/metrics.json with claim-keyed entries (C1-C8), results/per_seed.csv, and the RF confusion-matrix heatmap.
Write reproduce.py with --smoke / --variant / --seeds overrides; default invocation runs the full protocol.
Run `python reproduce.py --smoke` and confirm metrics.json appears with all keys, no NaN, and a test-set size of ~400 for the 2,000-row subsample.
Run the full protocol `python reproduce.py`. Expect ~15 minutes.
Inspect results/metrics.json: check C1 against the 98.9-100.0 band for the paper_order variant, note the leak-free variant's lower number as the honest bound, and record the C8 mismatch explanation.
smoke_test: `python reproduce.py --smoke` — stratified 2,000-row subsample of the cleaned frame, n_estimators=10 for both models, single seed 42, paper_order variant only. Proves: CSV loads, label auto-detects, dropna/encode/scale/SMOTE/split all run (test size ~400 with both classes), both models fit and predict, and results/metrics.json + results/per_seed.csv are written with all five metrics as finite floats. Expected runtime < 90 s.
intermediate_checks: Raw shape assertion: 101,174 rows x (17-21) columns; label column has exactly 8,830 positives and 92,344 negatives (fraud ratio 8.7%, imbalance 10.5:1) — R6/A6 validation; print the real column list next to the paper's 17 attributes and record any mismatch.
Missing-value audit: number of rows dropped by dropna and which columns drive it; assert a non-trivial but not catastrophic drop (report exact count into metrics.json).
Identifier check: assert 'phone number' has nunique == n_rows before dropping it; assert no remaining feature has nunique == n_rows.
Post-scaling check: every feature has min 0.0 and max 1.0 (tolerance 1e-9), no NaN/inf, dtype float64 (R2).
Post-SMOTE check: class counts exactly equal (sampling_strategy=1.0) and total rows == 2 * majority count (expected ~184,688); confirm synthetic rows were added only to the minority class.
Split check: len(X_test) == round(0.2 * n_total) for paper_order (expected ~36,938) and round(0.2 * n_clean) for leakfree (~20,235); both classes present in y_test with counts printed (R4/A7).

Sanity baselines BEFORE the full run: DummyClassifier most_frequent on the balanced test set (accuracy ~50%) and a single DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=5)/LogisticRegression (~90-97% expected) — confirms the features carry signal and the metric code is not inverted.
Metric-code unit test: feed a hand-built y_true/y_pred pair into evaluate() and assert accuracy/precision/recall/F1/confusion counts match the hand computation exactly (guards R8/R9).
Positive-class check: explicitly confirm fraud=1 is used as pos_label in precision/recall/F1/roc_auc, and that the RF confusion matrix prints in the same TP/TN/FP/FN orientation as Fig. 4.
Parameter/scale check: print n_features, n_train, n_test, RF n_estimators and observed max tree depth, so the C1 number can be interpreted against A3.
budget_plan: ~20 min total. Setup (3 min): pip install imbalanced-learn/xgboost, locate or download the 8 MB CSV, confirm it loads. Smoke (1.5 min): 2,000-row, 10-tree run through both models to validate the whole data flow and the metric code. Pre-flight checks (1.5 min): dataset shape/label counts, post-scale and post-SMOTE assertions, split sizes, dummy + shallow-tree baselines. Full run (12 min): 2 variants x 5 seeds x 2 models on the full preprocessed data — the dominant cost is 10 RF fits (~60 s each on ~148k x 17 train rows) and 10 XGB fits (~60-90 s each), with SMOTE (~30 s) run once per (variant, seed). Reporting (2 min): aggregate, write results/metrics.json + per_seed.csv + confusion-matrix figure, print the C1-C8 comparison against the tolerance band. If the machine proves slower than expected, fall back to seeds [42, 43, 44] and note the reduced repeat count in metrics.json rather than dropping the leak-free variant.
